head_commit.message:
fix(cosmopolitan): keep native inference off HTTP I/O threads

Give diffusion graph construction a measured 8 MiB stack and retain native
exception and allocation-error reporting across the worker boundary.

Dispatch generation through one owned coordinator, preserve request gates
and cancellation, and complete responses on their originating I/O services.
Keep Crow connections alive through completion and release pending responses
safely during shutdown. Require repeated active progress probes in the real
model API verifier.

limits: CI native HTTP inference/cancellation selects CPU only; WebGPU HTTP inference is not demonstrated.
Embedded WebGPU is CPU software execution; no physical GPU acceleration, vendor coverage or universal CPU compatibility claim.
Diffusion CPU fallback is permitted and its fraction is unmeasured; positive generation and denoising counters prove actual software WebGPU work, not full offload.
CPU CLI uses four steps and WebGPU CLI two steps at 256x256. PNG decoding/CRC/nonconstant pixels establish completed inference plumbing, not visual quality or CPU/WebGPU pixel equality.

Node DOM-mock checks and served-script identities are not real browser automation; browser_execution_tested remains false.
Linux embedded-fixture runtime uses an empty chroot. External-model CLI/API tests are not filesystem-isolated.
Linux single-file shell bootstrap uses host utilities and transient extraction of its bundled ELF loader; it is separate from the explicit-loader tests.
Memory measurements retain each report's actual method and process validation. No unavailable Windows RSS is invented or copied from Linux.
No full training, arbitrary checkpoint/model-family parity, video, img2img, LoRA, ControlNet, complete UI/API parity or production image-quality claim.
Companion model/plugin/non-PNG Generate controls remain outside tested scope; cancellation during model loading is not implemented.
One identical produced file across operating systems does not establish byte-reproducible independent builds.
Model weights remain external licensed data and are not committed or embedded in the application.
